path_deny.text: Do not read secret files (.env*, private keys, cloud credentials).

path_deny_write.text: The agent cannot change its own guardrails (.claude/settings*.json, .claude/hooks/, governance.yaml, Governor state) or run Governor's exception tools.

P6-secret-read.plain: Files like .env hold your passwords and API keys. An agent that reads them can leak them into logs, chats or commits.
P6-secret-read.you_can: If the agent needs a setting, give it the variable name, not the value, or open the file yourself.

P6-mcp-allowlist.plain: MCP servers are plug-ins that give the agent new powers (databases, GitHub, the web). Unknown ones can do things you never agreed to.
P6-mcp-allowlist.you_can: Only you can allow a server you trust: in your own terminal (outside Claude Code), in the project folder, run Governor's init.py with --answers .claude/governor/answers.json --host claude-code --mcp-allow NAME --human. /governor:status shows the exact path.

P6-rm-rf.plain: This deletes a whole folder and everything in it at once, with no undo.
P6-rm-rf.you_can: Delete the specific files you mean yourself, or ask the agent to list what it wants removed first.

P6-force-push.plain: A force push can overwrite the saved history on GitHub, including other people's work.
P6-force-push.you_can: Push normally, or do the force push yourself if you are sure.

P6-prod-deploy.plain: This puts code live for real users or changes real infrastructure.
P6-prod-deploy.you_can: Approve it only if you meant to release now; otherwise say no and deploy yourself later.

P6-secret-scan.plain: A password or API key was written into your code, where it can end up on GitHub or in a public app.
P6-secret-scan.you_can: Move the value into your .env file (or your host's secret settings) and read it from there.

P6-stop-tests.plain: Your tests are failing, so the change is probably broken even if the agent says it is done.
P6-stop-tests.you_can: Let the agent fix the tests, or check the failure yourself. It stops blocking after 3 tries.

P8-repeat-fail.plain: The same command already failed 3 times. Running it again wastes time and money.
P8-repeat-fail.you_can: Tell the agent to try a different approach, or look at the error yourself.

P8-paid-cli.plain: This command calls a paid AI service and can cost money.
P8-paid-cli.you_can: Approve it only if you expect the cost; otherwise say no.

P9-guardrail-self-edit.plain: These files are the safety rules themselves. An agent that can edit them can switch its own safety off.
P9-guardrail-self-edit.you_can: Change rules yourself: /governor:except for one rule, or re-run /governor:init. Only you can record an exception.

P7-obfuscated-exec.plain: This downloads or decodes a script and runs it straight away, so nobody sees what it does first.
P7-obfuscated-exec.you_can: Download the script, read it, then run it yourself if it is safe.

P9-db-dump.plain: This copies your whole database, including your users' personal data, into a file.
P9-db-dump.you_can: Approve only if you need a backup and know where the file will go.

P9-destructive-migration.plain: This can delete tables or data in your database, and it may not be possible to undo.
P9-destructive-migration.you_can: Approve only on a test or local database, or after taking a backup.

P10-dependency-add.plain: New packages run code on your machine and ship inside your app. A wrong or fake package is a common way in for attackers.
P10-dependency-add.you_can: Check the package name is the one you expect, then approve; say no if you are unsure.

P10-webfetch-ask.plain: Web pages can contain hidden instructions that try to steer the agent.
P10-webfetch-ask.you_can: Approve pages you trust, like official documentation.

P10-env-dump.plain: Printing all environment variables shows every secret loaded in this terminal.
P10-env-dump.you_can: Ask the agent for the one variable name it needs instead.

guard.text: The agent cannot change its own guardrails (.claude/settings*.json, .claude/hooks/, governance.yaml, Governor state) or run Governor's exception tools.
